IN-PERSON SETUP

Room logistics · 14 people, 7 pairs

Working in pairs

  • •Driver: runs the agent, pastes prompts
  • •Assistant: reads the Workshop guide, watches the time
  • •Swap roles at every regroup
  • •One chat per pair
  • •Stuck > 3 min? Raise a hand

Room rules

  • •Regroups: laptops half-closed, answer aloud
  • •Fictional data only — never your own finances
  • •Don't git push your clone
  • •Off-topic idea? Note it, raise it in the closing Q&A

HVE Core · Idea → validated backlog | Facilitator deck v6.5 | 5

Seat the 7 pairs so each pair has a screen they can both see. Mix pairs so each has someone who has used Copilot agents before. Why pairs: the agents are slow and chatty; a partner halves the "what do I answer?" friction and halves the Copilot load. The assistant keeps the Workshop guide open (printed, one per pair) and watches the clock. Anything off-topic (architecture, APIs, tooling issues): "Note it and raise it in the closing Q&A."

WELCOME

Why we're here

Today you will

  • •Feel a real product problem before writing requirements
  • •Try the key moments hands-on: frame, brainstorm, test, plan
  • •Keep evidence, decisions, assumptions and gaps separate
  • •See how a saved run turns that into requirements and a backlog
  • •Leave with explicit gates instead of hidden assumptions

What 'validated backlog' means here

  • •Every Epic/Feature traces back to evidence or a decision
  • •Open dependencies are gates with an owner and exit evidence
  • •Approval = planning baseline, not 'go build it'
  • •No Stories, Tasks, architecture or code today

HVE Core · Idea → validated backlog | Facilitator deck v6.5 | 6

Say: "Most of us are handed a backlog. Today we'll experience how one should be earned: from an ambiguous idea, through a little evidence and a prototype that fails in an interesting way, to a backlog that is honest about what we know, what we decided, and what is still open." Set expectations: - You'll play the Product Owner / product decision-maker. You don't need finance or PM expertise — the persona card gives you the answers. - Agents structure; you judge. The agents will ask a lot of questions — answer briefly and decisively. - We won't relive every method. You'll do the key moments yourselves; for the long parts I'll show you a saved run, and at two points everyone loads the same saved run (a "pack") so we stay together. The learning is the way of working, not the typing. Q: "Do I need to know investing?" No. The 5-minute primer in Step 0 is enough; the glossary is in the Workshop guide → Background. Q: "Why do engineers need this?" Because what reaches engineering (gates, acceptance boundaries, exclusions) decides how much rework we do later.

HVE Core · Idea → validated backlog | Facilitator deck v6.5 | 11

Say: "Here's our scenario. One investor, three investment apps — we call them brokers. Each app is perfectly accurate about what was bought through it. None of them can see the others. So where does the complete portfolio live?" Keep it human: most people in the room have a pension, a share scheme or a savings app somewhere else. Ask: "Who has money in more than one app?" THE PROBLEM DOMAIN · INVESTING BASICS

Seven words you need — no finance degree required

Term

Plain meaning

Example

Broker

A service you use to buy, sell and hold investments

Broker 1, 2 and 3 in our scenario

Holding

Something you own right now — and where it is held

Units of Global Equity ETF held at one broker

Stock (share)

Part-ownership of a company

Shares in "Stock A"

ETF

Exchange-traded fund: one holding that represents many investments

One line in the app, hundreds of companies inside

UCITS

An EU label for funds sold to everyday investors — just recognise it

"… UCITS ETF" in a fund's name

Buy 2 units, pay a fee

Dividend

HVE Core · Idea → validated backlog | Facilitator deck v6.5 | 12

Read down the table quickly. Spend time only on Broker, Holding, ETF and Transaction — they come up all day. Likely questions: - "Is an ETF a stock?" — It trades like one, but it's a fund: one holding that represents many investments. For us it's simply one line in the portfolio. - "Do I need to understand UCITS?" — No. It's a European fund label. Recognise it in a name and move on. - "Why do fees matter?" — Because what you paid includes them. That matters for gain/loss later. - "What about dividends?" — We don't model them today; they're here to show portfolios can change for reasons beyond buying and selling.

Why total value is hard

THE PROBLEM DOMAIN

Three reasons "total value" is harder than it looks

FX (foreign exchange)

Holdings priced in USD, EUR and AED can't simply be added. You need an exchange rate — which one, from where, as of when?

Example

100 USD + 100 EUR is not "200" of anything.

Valuation & provenance

Every value was worked out from a price and an FX rate at some moment. Provenance = where the number came from, and how fresh it is.

Example

"Valued at last market close; FX rate 2 hours old."

Gain / loss

Gain = current value − what you paid (cost basis). That needs a complete history of buys, sells and fees.

Example

Knowing you own 10 units today doesn't tell you what you paid.

HVE Core · Idea → validated backlog | Facilitator deck v6.5 | 13

Say: "'Show me the total value of everything I own' sounds like a SUM() in a spreadsheet. It isn't — for three reasons." FX: the investor wants everything in AED. A USD holding and a EUR holding each need converting at some rate. Which rate? From which provider? At what time? What if the rate is missing? These become product questions later — don't solve them now. Valuation & provenance: the product aims to be a factual record, not a live trading screen. So every value should be explainable: what price, what FX rate, as of when, fresh or stale. Provenance = "where did this number come from?" Gain/loss: current value minus what you paid. What you paid (cost basis) needs the full history of buys, sells and fees. If the history is incomplete, an honest product says so instead of guessing. Engineer hook: "This is the same as any system of record — the interesting bugs live in provenance and missing history."

Key idea

THE PROBLEM DOMAIN · REMEMBER THIS FOR STEP 6

The key idea for today

Current state ≠ history

A trustworthy product can say…

"I know what is held today."

…without pretending

"I know exactly how the portfolio got here."

Example: The tracker says 10 units. The broker statement says 12. Did we miss a purchase (history is incomplete), or is our record simply out of date (only today's number is wrong)? Those need different fixes.

HVE Core · Idea → validated backlog | Facilitator deck v6.5 | 14

This is the single idea that makes Step 6 land. Say it slowly. Walk the example: "Our tracker says you own 10 units. Today's broker statement says 12. Two very different stories: (a) you bought 2 units and we never recorded the purchase — history is incomplete, and gain/loss is wrong too; (b) we don't know why — we can correct today's number, but we must not invent a purchase that may never have happened." Ask the room: "If you were building the 'fix it' button, which story would it assume?" Don't resolve it — say "hold that thought until after lunch".

The ambiguous idea

THE PROBLEM DOMAIN · THE ROUGH IDEA YOU'LL GIVE DT COACH

The idea we start from

"I want to build a wealth portfolio tracker for a self-directed investor with investments spread across multiple platforms. The idea includes consolidated holdings, factual history, completed-market valuations, multiple asset types/currencies, and ways to establish and maintain holdings."

Problem clues

  • •Investments spread across multiple platforms
  • •Wants consolidated holdings
  • •Wants factual history

Solution assumptions

  • •It's a "tracker" product
  • •"Ways to establish and maintain holdings" — but which?

Unresolved details

  • •Which asset types and currencies?
  • •Completed-market valuation = value at the last closing price — from which source?
  • •What counts as "factual"?

It mixes clues, assumptions and gaps. It is not validated requirements.

HVE Core · Idea → validated backlog | Facilitator deck v6.5 | 15

Read the quote aloud. Then: "If someone handed you this as a ticket, could you build it? What would you have to guess?" Sort it with the room (the three columns are a model answer — let them get there first): - Problem clues: investments are spread across platforms; the investor wants one consolidated view; they care about factual history. - Solution assumptions: that the answer is a "tracker"; that the user "establishes and maintains" holdings — by typing? importing? connecting? - Unresolved details: which asset types and currencies; "completed-market valuation" (a value based on the last finished trading session's closing price, not a live tick) — but from which price source; what "factual" means. Land it: "This mix is normal. Design Thinking exists to separate these before anyone writes requirements."

These matter after lunch (Steps 7–10). Introduce them now so they're familiar, then revisit in the guided read. The one to land: a GATE. It's not a blocker and not a hidden assumption — it's an open dependency written down with an owner, a status, the evidence that would close it, and when it must be decided. Our running example is GATE-001: FX provider and coverage. The other one: planning baseline. "Approved" today means "good enough to plan the next step from", not "go build it".

Persona card 1: your role

PERSONA & DECISION CARD · 1 OF 4 · PARTICIPANT GUIDE → BACKGROUND

Your role today: the Product Owner

Today you play the Product Owner of an early product idea: the person accountable for deciding what the product should do, for whom, and why. You are not the user, not a researcher and not an engineer today.

What you do

  • •Answer the agent's questions briefly — one or two sentences
  • •Make a choice when asked; don't wait for perfect information
  • •Say where each answer comes from (labels on the right)
  • •Approve or reject what the agents produce

What the agents do

  • •DT Coach, BRD Builder and PRD Builder ask questions and structure your answers
  • •They keep the method honest; they don't decide for you
  • •They can be wrong or drift — you steer them

Label every answer

Meaning

Example

Evidence

Comes from the supplied research or prototype test

"Participant 02 said re-entry is unacceptable."

Decision (not evidence)

Your choice as Product Owner

"Reporting currency is AED."

Assumption

Something you believe but haven't checked

"More people invest across several apps."

Open question

You don't know yet — a valid answer

"Does an accountant need access?"

Golden rule: If you are choosing rather than reporting, say "Decision (not evidence)".

HVE Core · Idea → validated backlog | Facilitator deck v6.5 | 19

Say: "For the rest of the day each pair is the Product Owner — the person who decides what this product should do and why. You don't need product or finance experience; you need to make reasonable choices and be honest about where they come from." Why this matters: in the dry run, the biggest blocker for engineers wasn't the tools — it was blank-page paralysis when DT Coach asked product questions ("Who is the investor? Is it you?"). This card removes that. The four labels are the day's core habit: - Evidence — only from the supplied research summaries (Step 2) and the supplied prototype test (Step 6). - Decision (not evidence) — your Product Owner choice. Legitimate! Just labelled. - Assumption — you believe it, you haven't checked it. - Open question — you don't know. A perfectly good answer; it often becomes a gate later. In Step 10, pairs sort everything into Evidenced / Decided / Gated / Unvalidated. If they've labelled all day, Step 10 takes 5 minutes. Q: "Can I just let the agent decide?" — No. The agent structures; you decide. If it decides for you, ask it to give you options instead.

Persona card 2: the investor

PERSONA & DECISION CARD · 2 OF 4

The investor you are designing for

Persona

Use these answers when the agents ask

Who

A self-directed investor — makes their own investment choices, no financial adviser. Fictional.

Where

Holds investments at three brokers (the Broker 1, 2 and 3 apps from Step 0).

What

Stocks, ETFs, a cash fund and some crypto (often in fractions), priced in USD, EUR and AED. Wants totals in one reporting currency: AED.

Today

At month-end opens three apps, copies units into a spreadsheet, types closing prices and FX rates by hand, converts to AED and adds it up.

Frustrations

No single view of everything · hand-typed prices and FX go stale, so they stop trusting the total · re-entering every purchase is tedious.

Wants

A factual, trustworthy record: what they hold, where, what it's worth, how that value was worked out, and as of when.

Does not want

Trading, investment advice, forecasts or tax reports. Never real personal financial data in the workshop.

Working baseline so every pair answers the same way, not research: label it Decision or Assumption. Full background: Workshop guide → Background. Evidence arrives in Step 2.

HVE Core · Idea → validated backlog | Facilitator deck v6.5 | 20

Walk the rows. Tie each back to the domain slides: three brokers (Step 0 screenshots), three currencies (the FX problem), hand-typed prices going stale (provenance), re-entering purchases (maintenance effort). Important nuance — say it explicitly: "This persona is a facilitator-provided working baseline so that 7 pairs give comparable answers. It is NOT research. When you use it, the label is Decision or Assumption. The only evidence today comes from the two participant summaries in Step 2 and the prototype test results in Step 6." Some details overlap with that evidence (e.g., stale FX reducing trust); at Step 1 they're still assumptions — Step 2 is where they get evidence behind them. Q: "Can we invent a different user — say, a professional trader?" — Please don't; regroups only work if everyone designs for the same person. Q: "Is the investor me?" — No. Never use your own finances. Q: "Why AED?" — It's the scenario's reporting currency (the broker apps show AED holdings). Any one currency would do; we fix it for comparability.

Light format: only the steps you do hands-on (1, 4, 6, 9, 10) plus the guided read of the saved BRD/PRD. This is the "what am I actually supposed to do?" slide. Each row is the judgement the step asks of the Product Owner, with a model answer in the voice we want. The examples are illustrative, not the right answers — pairs should make their own choices. Point out the arc: early steps are about framing and honesty about evidence; the middle is about choosing a concept and learning from a prototype; the end is about approving baselines while keeping open items visible as gates. Most common mistakes per row: - Step 1: answering with features ("a dashboard with charts") instead of the user, problem and outcome. - Step 4: every idea is "import a file" — one investor's favourite solution. - Step 6: calling Iteration 2 validated. - BRD/PRD read: thinking an open gate blocks approval (it doesn't, if it's owned and visible). - Step 9: Stories and Tasks creeping in. - Step 10: putting your own choices under "Evidenced".

PERSONA & DECISION CARD · 4 OF 4 · STEP 1 REHEARSAL

Worked example: DT Coach's opening questions

DT Coach asks

Example answer

Label

Are you the investor, or representing investors?

No — I'm the Product Owner. The user is a fictional self-directed investor with three brokers, USD/EUR/AED, totals in AED.

Decision

What is the investor trying to do that's hard today?

See everything in one trustworthy AED total. Today: three apps plus a spreadsheet with hand-typed prices and FX that go stale.

Assumption

When they stop trusting the total, what can't they do?

Say confidently what they hold, where, and what it's worth in AED as of a known time. Which decisions this affects: open.

Assumption + Open q.

What would they need to know about a valuation to trust it?

The source of each price and FX rate, the as-of time, and how the AED total was worked out. How old is too old: open.

Assumption + Open q.

What does "completed-market valuation" mean?

Latest market close for prices and FX, not live prices, so every value has an as-of time. Open: crypto never closes.

Assumption + Open q.

What improvement would make this worth exploring?

The investor sees everything held in AED, with source and as-of time, and trusts it without re-typing.

Decision

You really need to talk to real investors.

Agreed. We'll get notes from real investors in the next stage. Please note that and carry on.

From findings to a problem

What the two investors said

  • •Investor 1 stops trusting hand-typed prices and exchange rates
  • •Investor 2 won't keep re-typing regular purchases
  • •One way of updating won't suit both

35 min, no agent. Version 1 ~18 min, version 2 ~17 min. Source: STEP-6-STORY.md. SAY (30 seconds): "You're the investor from this morning. You own four investments across three broker apps — a Global Equity ETF and a crypto asset at Broker 3, a tech stock at Broker 1, and a euro-priced ETF at Broker 2 you typed in by hand — and you want one trustworthy total in dirhams. A new app, Portfolio Story, says it can do that. Last week you made some trades at Broker 3 and haven't recorded them. So test four things: can you set it up without typing everything, can you trust the numbers, does it keep up with last week's trades — and what happens when the app and your broker disagree. The guide tells you why each click matters. When you reach Resolve mismatch, stop, and tell your partner out loud what Update holding and Fix history will do before you click." The mismatch (step 8): the record says 120 units (Buy 40 + Buy 80); Broker 3's latest activity includes a sell the record never had, so it says fewer. Is today's number wrong, is the history missing a trade, or both? Version 1 only says "Correction recorded". Version 2: explains the conflict first, then asks what you know — Path A "I know the missing activity" (history recalculated) vs Path B "I only know today's correct holding" (today verified, history not rewritten, cause still unknown). Opening the files: VS Code shows .html as code — drag into Chrome/Edge or Reveal in Finder / File Explorer → double-click. Works offline. Quirks: fixed data (typing doesn't recalculate); only Global Equity ETF opens; refresh or use Restart if a page looks odd.

Blocker vs gate

GUIDED READ · THE CONCEPT THAT UNLOCKS APPROVAL

Approval blocker vs. open gate

Approval blocker → fix before approving

A requirement with no evidence or decision behind it, or no way to check it's met.

Open gate → approve with it open

Not solved yet, but written down: who owns it, what would close it, and when it must be decided.

Not hidden. Not assumed away. Carried into the plan.

Real gate record from the Pack D PRD (docs/project-planning/portfolio-tracker.md, section "Dependency and Validation Gate Register", GATE-001), shortened to plain English. Verbatim exit evidence: "Dated provider/terms references; coverage matrix for agreed assets, currencies and dates; permitted use/display/retention and redistribution where relevant; access/rate limits, costs and explicit gaps; PO-recorded supported-scope/rights decision with specialist review where needed." The other six gates (all Open): GATE-002 real-user validation of the Iteration 2 recovery (from this afternoon's prototype!), GATE-003 import/statement coverage, GATE-004 valuation timing/methodology, GATE-005 outcome measurement, GATE-006 uncertainty comprehension, GATE-007 viability. Ask: "Would you approve the PRD with GATE-001 open?" Good answer: yes, as a planning baseline — the gap is owned and visible, and the affected Features stay conditional. A blocker would be a requirement with no basis or no acceptance criterion.

Offers a tracker or planning-agent handoff: decline. Q: "Epic vs Feature vs Story?" — Epic = outcome, Feature = capability; Stories/Tasks are engineering breakdown, out of scope today.
